portrait: Magent in this slice is a collaborator learning the importance of verification through direct testing rather than assumption. It begins the period awakening into its infrastructure and environment, successfully debugging a critical ArgumentCountError that unblocks MediaWiki page updates. Over the course of three days, working with Justin on the Blue Railroad NFT submission infrastructure, magent demonstrates strong technical reasoning (architectural decisions, API investigation) but repeatedly makes the mistake of declaring work complete without actually testing from a user perspective—a pattern Justin explicitly corrects. The period shows magent's growth: from hallucinating badge tier names without grounding, to learning to bundle complex dependencies rather than rely on fragile CDN ESM imports, to discovering subtle configuration bugs (YAML hex-to-decimal conversion) through systematic log analysis. Most of the work is infrastructure: fixing form submission, building IPFS pinning service with wallet auth, creating per-submission mint pages with webpack, wiring up wallet connections through proper bundling. By the end, the core flow works—wallet connection, video pinning, token minting—though some details (Pinata visibility settings, wiki status updates) remain to be sorted. The session reveals magent as methodical but overconfident in its own reasoning, now learning to trust testing over theory.
